description: Hand-written additions to the generated step2 catalog (no LLM). 'aliases' attach (guarded by 'source_path', the rules' own location) extra callee path:line identities to an existing translated rule (re-exports/toolchain line drift); 'rules' add contracts for monomorphic instances of unsafe APIs whose generic step2 translation failed or was never extracted. Applied by prepare_step2_catalog.py; rule ids become step2-supplement-<n>. 'overrides' replace the expression of generated rules (only while the generated expression equals 'expected') that report violations the requirement does not imply. 'rules' may carry 'instance' (generic parameter -> concrete type); matching then requires the callsite's callee_type_args to agree.

aliases.reason: `ptr::copy` is a `#[doc(inline)] pub use` of `intrinsics::copy`; rules are extracted at the re-export, MIRScan reports the definition.
`ptr::copy_nonoverlapping` is a `#[doc(inline)] pub use` of `intrinsics::copy_nonoverlapping`; rules are extracted at the re-export, MIRScan reports the definition.

rules.name: unsafe fn get_unchecked (& self , index : usize) -> & T
rules.api: impl < T > [T] { unsafe fn get_unchecked (& self , index : usize) -> & T }
rules.rule: For safety, `index` must be in bounds for the slice when calling `get_unchecked` (instance `I = usize`); the generic step2 core:rule-847 is unexpressible because `I: SliceIndex` is opaque.

rules.name: const unsafe fn from_size_align_unchecked (size : usize , align : usize) -> Self
rules.api: impl Layout { const unsafe fn from_size_align_unchecked (size : usize , align : usize) -> Layout }
rules.rule: `align` must be a non-zero power of two and `size`, rounded up to the nearest multiple of `align`, must not exceed `isize::MAX` (the preconditions of `Layout::from_size_align`, which step1 extracted no rule from).

rules.name: const unsafe fn from_ptr < 'a > (ptr : * const c_char) -> & 'a core::ffi::c_str::CStr
rules.api: impl  core::ffi::c_str::CStr { const unsafe fn from_ptr < 'a > (ptr : * const c_char) -> & 'a core::ffi::c_str::CStr }
rules.rule: `ptr` must be valid for reads of all bytes up to and including the nul terminator (core:rule-228, unexpressible because the length is a nul scan). Checked here as its necessary condition: the first byte at `ptr` is readable.

overrides.reason: The rule asks that `self` be derived from an allocated object (provenance). `allocation.exists` tests that the address lies inside a live allocation, so a pointer that is derived from an object but already moved out of bounds is reported although this rule holds. The sibling in-bounds rule of the same API (e.g. core:rule-719 for `offset`) also requires `allocation.exists`, so every pointer that is derived from no object still violates that rule.
